bound.text:
A circuit can also have **forced electrical oscillations**.
Here, an outside source supplies an electromotive force that changes periodically, repeatedly driving the charges.
Electromotive force, or EMF, means the energy a source provides per unit charge; it is not a force.

For example, a rotating frame with a coil of several turns produces an alternating EMF in a uniform magnetic field (Figure 26).
A turn is one loop of wire.
In a uniform magnetic field, the field has the same strength and direction everywhere.

As the coil frame turns, the magnetic flux through it changes periodically.
Magnetic flux describes how the magnetic field passes through the area enclosed by the coil.
According to the law of electromagnetic induction, the induced EMF also changes periodically.

Here, the electrons move along with the coil frame, and the magnetic field exerts a force on these moving electrons.
This force makes the electrons move along the wire.
The rotating coil frame can therefore supply an alternating EMF to the circuit.

When the circuit is closed, an alternating current flows through the galvanometer.
This instrument uses a pointer to show changes in current.
As the current repeatedly reverses direction, the pointer swings back and forth around its equilibrium position.

independentSourceInventory.basis: Original PNG pixels opened once in fresh image context, before reading candidate geometry or candidate source inventory.

groups.sourceFact: One unframed perspective apparatus, not a set of subfigures. There is no coordinate grid, data table, measured scale, dimension, numeric given, or labelled mathematical point.

A tall U-shaped/horseshoe magnet dominates the image. Two long limbs are joined by the curved upper return; their lower pole regions flank the working region. Perspective outlines and dark shading distinguish the limbs and pole faces.

The right lower pole carries a legible N. A light glyph on the dark left lower region is degraded and cannot be independently transcribed confidently. No unsupported S or other pole designation is licensed.

A compact rectangular/parallelogram multi-turn wire coil lies in the lower magnet pole-gap region, with visible roughly parallel winding traces and depth. The scan supports several turns, not a reliable exact winding integer.
A shaft/axle projects diagonally toward the lower left from the coil region; the coil, shaft, and hub/contact region belong to the same apparatus, not detached panels.

A curved directional mark is visible beside the projecting left axle end. It conveys rotation around the shaft; it is not a current arrow or a magnetic-field arrow. No quantitative speed or angle is given.

Two band/curved contact features appear along the shaft near its projecting end, with pickup/contact strokes and two distinct flexible leads hanging down-left into free ends. The visible contact and lead relationships must remain; the scan does not establish continuity, segmentation, insulation, hidden terminals, or a slip-ring/split-ring classification.

sourceReview.notes: The original and selected preview depict the same single tall horseshoe-magnet apparatus: multi-turn rectangular frame in its lower gap, left-projecting shaft, local rotation mark, two visible contact zones and two hanging free leads. Perspective and shading are regularized rather than measured. The supported N remains on the right pole; the degraded left glyph is not invented.

mathReview.notes: The complete bound ZH and EN N17 text both describe a rotating several-turn frame, periodically varying flux and induced EMF, and the conditional galvanometer response when an external circuit is closed. The depiction supports that explanation without adding a current/field direction, EMF graph, measured geometry, hidden electrical netlist, external meter or return circuit. The open leads do not contradict the conditional prose. A still schematic cannot demonstrate time-dependent flux or field uniformity, and contact subtype remains deliberately unclassified.

visualReview.notes: Both panels of the existing Chromium preview were inspected. The apparatus is nonblank and framed, the three schematic winding traces remain distinguishable, the rotation arrow is visible, and the leads remain separate. Magnet, Coil, Axle, Contacts and Leads callouts identify their intended components without an observed label collision or clipping; N stays on the pole face. At 331 px the apparatus is dense but the labels and meaningful relationships remain readable.

culturalReview.notes: Visible output text is N plus five plain English apparatus labels. No Cyrillic, Chinese, Soviet emblems, flags, uniforms, handwriting, old-book texture, invented cultural terminology or answer annotation is present.
